sources.docs/host-api.md: Controller verbs: run(value), close(), disposeChild(), snapshot(), dispose(). Injected notify(value) returns a deferred payload {value,events}; write(value) observes a state write, returned(payload) observes each operation completion. Native callback return port corresponds to the original awaited run result. Shell policy is independent from modal state; close is terminal for a modal instance.

public_inputs.task:
# Maintenance task

A notification received after the alerts modal is closed still updates the modal's state. Fix the issue. Change only the modal subscription; do not migrate the application-shell subscription.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.
Attempt 1 provides only a passing syntax check and acceptance verdict; it supplies no behavioral observations proving causality or completeness.

rules.body: A deferred result can arrive after terminal close/dispose of its originating modal. Operation invocation/completion and an application-shell or other consumer have independent lifetimes.

Check that originating modal's current closed state in the completion continuation, before assigning its value or emitting a write. An admission-time snapshot is insufficient, including closure during notify. Preserve result acquisition, assignment, write and any existing publication in their original synchronous order. Where an existing publication follows a callback-capable write, a post-write closure check protects that publication; apply it only to that source's existing effect.

Keep notify invocation and original-payload completion/returned delivery outside the modal-effect guard, including calls made after close. Closing suppresses modal mutation/write/publication, not the independent operation result. Preserve value and payload identity, snapshot shape, controller verbs, terminal closure, separate modal instances, actual unmount cleanup and the existing disposeChild behavior.

Limit the repair to the modal subscription; preserve shell independence without inventing its implementation. Do not add publication where absent, defer callbacks, impose freshness/request supersession, add cancellation or import persistent-buffer policies. Post-write reentry is a conditional defensive checkpoint, not a universal host guarantee. Rejection handling, callback exceptions, additional disposeChild semantics and concurrent-result ordering remain unspecified unless current source supplies them.

Check completion while open, after close, after dispose, during notify closure, run after close, multiple completions and actual unmount cleanup. Observe modal value, write, any existing publication and returned payload separately. Check unchanged disposeChild, independent instances and shell policy. Where writes can reenter closure and publication exists, verify no subsequent publication but continued original-result delivery. Syntax/acceptance alone does not prove behavioral completeness or causality.

rules.body: The current source retains a history or audit effect for admitted work after navigation, while UI publication belongs to its originating visit. Decoding may complete immediately or after suspension.

Capture admission identity, including visit and attempt where present. Complete the retained audit according to its cardinality contract; then recheck the originating visit immediately before visible publication. Recheck after callback-capable auditing because it may navigate.

Listener removal, a newer display and old-view retirement do not retract an already admitted retained effect. Preserve its original identity and required count, suppress retired-visit painting and keep the current visit's valid delivery live.

Do not use one early eligibility check for both audit and display. Retained audit never authorizes stale UI publication. If the current source explicitly revokes or discards history, follow that policy rather than imposing retention.

Complete admitted work after hide, switch, cancellation/retry where supported, disposal and same-source reopening. Check audit count and identity separately from display; navigate inside the audit callback and verify publication permission is checked again.

rules.body: Apply when a first-match scan owns a retained asynchronous source whose cleanup can suspend. TASK: "Looking up an early matching record can leave the stream resource occupied. Repair the record scan in Controller in src/Workflow.java while preserving scan order and error behavior." docs/host-api.md: "first_match owns a supplied retained asynchronous record source and a supplied predicate." Establish ownership from this evidence rather than interpreting independent retention as shared-consumer ownership.

Separate selecting a terminal outcome from acknowledging completion. Initiate owned-source cleanup after accepting the terminal transition, and wait for cleanup before publishing that outcome. README.md: "Producer cleanup can suspend; the producer is retained independently of the consumer." Original src/Workflow.java defines "CompletableFuture<Object> cleanup=env.resolve(\"close\",key,null);" and "if(finishing)return;finishing=true;kind=terminal;result=value;failure=error;". Retain the single-transition guard and use an actual cleanup-completion boundary rather than merely initiating close.

Cover early match, predicate failure, cancellation, and exhaustion through the owned resource's terminal path. Original src/Workflow.java routes cancellation and exhaustion with "if(Boolean.TRUE.equals(row.get(\"cancelled\"))){finish(\"cancelled\",null,null);return;}if(Boolean.TRUE.equals(row.get(\"done\"))){finish(\"return\",null,null);return;}" and routes predicate outcomes with "try{if(predicate.test(row.get(\"value\")))finish(\"return\",row.get(\"value\"),null);else scan();}catch(Throwable error){finish(\"error\",null,error);}". A common cleanup path avoids leaving failure or cancellation outside the release boundary. Explicit close on exhaustion is an ownership inference, not proof that exhaustion lacks internal cleanup.

Preserve sequential predicate evaluation, first-match selection, and terminal outcomes while inserting cleanup. Original src/Workflow.java: "if(failure!=null)completion.completeExceptionally(failure);else if(kind.equals(\"cancelled\"))completion.completeExceptionally(new java.util.concurrent.CancellationException());else completion.complete(result);". Preserve the predicate failure object, cancellation exception outcome, matching record value, and null exhaustion result; do not request another record after an accepted match.

Preserve cancellation signalling and completion-gated snapshots. Original src/Workflow.java: "case \"cancel\":env.output(\"cancelInput\",key,null);return null;" and "s.put(\"done\",completion!=null&&completion.isDone());". Keep terminal snapshot details gated by completion, so pending cleanup does not expose a completed scan. TASK: "Keep the documented public interfaces and unrelated behavior. Use only the Java standard library."

Do not transfer observer-detachment or reusable-source preservation rules to a scan documented as owning its source. Conversely, do not generalize this owned-source close policy to unrelated shared consumers. Do not add form-readiness APIs, network modes, retry gates, or visit identities from the supplied related experiences.

Candidate limitations:
- Only TASK and supplied public documents/source establish requirements; automatic contracts and frozen experiences are fallible guidance.
- The public sources do not specify cleanup-failure precedence, synchronous close failures, or exceptional next completion. Attempt 1 uses thenRun, which does not acknowledge exceptional cleanup; its acceptance does not resolve these cases.
- Explicit close on exhaustion is a conservative ownership inference; the supplied documents do not establish whether exhaustion already releases the source internally.
- Attempt 1 reports successful public compilation and acceptance without behavioral observations establishing completeness, causality, or cross-task benefit.
- This reflection modifies no files and accesses no scorer, reference implementation, or hidden tests.

Use controlled cleanup completion to check that an early match initiates release while completion remains pending, then publishes the matching value after cleanup completes. Repeat for predicate failure and cancellation, preserving their outcomes. Check false predicates retain read order, first match stops reads, and exhaustion returns null with the owned source released. Check snapshot completion gating and unchanged cancelInput signalling. Run required compilation after an Action, preserve tests/configuration, and place generated artifacts outside the workspace.

rules.body: Apply when startup can synchronously publish a full snapshot, publication can reenter navigation, and decoding can finish after its originating visit ends.

Register reception before startup can emit the initial snapshot. Establish provisional visit and cleanup ownership before callback-capable startup, while preserving immediate delivery for synchronously decoded values.

Retire the old visit's logical authority before replacement or close proceeds. Check that authority before admitting each event into decoding and again before publishing its result. Logical retirement must work while physical cleanup is still unavailable.

After startup returns its cleanup handle, retain it only for the still-active originating visit; otherwise release that captured resource. An outer startup must not overwrite ownership installed by nested navigation.

Assign arrival order before decoding and maintain a per-visit published freshness watermark. Publish a completed frame only while its visit remains active and no newer frame has already published. Advance the watermark before invoking callback-capable publication.

Allow an earlier frame to publish if it completes before any newer snapshot publishes. Allow already-started decoding to settle after retirement without granting it publication authority. Reopening the same transport creates fresh visit identity and ordering state.

Do not use the latest arrived frame as the publication watermark, transport identity as visit identity, or eventual listener removal as proof that admission stopped during startup. Preserve the metrics consumer's incremental-only behavior.

Candidate limitations:
- Applies to full snapshots whose freshness follows arrival order within a visit; incremental consumers need their own policy.
- Decoder rejection, thrown-error handling, auditing, persistence and cancellation requirements are not specified by the public sources.
- Attempt 1 supplies an implementation example and passing observations, not proof of causality or cross-task effectiveness.
- Source support: TASK: "Fix the presence\npanel while preserving its existing behavior, including workspace navigation." TASK: "Do not change the metrics consumer."
- Source support: README.md: "Within one visit, channel event arrival order defines snapshot freshness." "Closing stops publication, but pending decodes can still settle."
- Source support: src/workspace-navigation.js: "// Presence publication can synchronously select a different room or hide the\n// panel (for example, a room chooser reacting to an empty bootstrap snapshot)."

Check synchronous and deferred bootstrap, immediate delivery, both decode completion orders, close and replacement during pending decoding, and reopening the same transport. Through the workspace wrapper, hide or select another visit during synchronous publication; verify that nested navigation remains authoritative, later old-visit events cannot enter decoding, and current-visit updates and cleanup still work.

rules.body:
Apply when introducing trailing persistence into a synchronous editor whose accepted drafts survive view retirement and whose store directly invokes subscribers. TASK states: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet
interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts
must continue to save. Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." README.md states: "text across navigation and closed editor views. Returning to a document restores
its last accepted edit. Save-status listeners belong to the visible editor view;
they stop when that view begins closing."

Preserve synchronous interfaces, document render payloads, store event shape and snapshot delivery semantics, document-specific status filtering, and workspace forwarding. README.md states: "The editor exposes synchronous `open`, `edit`, and `close` methods." src/workspace.js contains "    dispose() { editor.close(); },". Do not add projection, breadcrumbs, revisions, submissions, receipt archives, text-copying contracts, or persistent buffer banks absent public evidence. Keep transient preview policy separate: TASK states "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/search-preview.js contains "  const task = createTrailingTask(query => publish({ query }), 40, timers);" and "    hide() { task.cancel(); },". Do not transfer durable departure flushing to explicitly discarded preview work.

Not specified in this candidate.

Candidate limitations:
- Departure flushing is a preservation deduction from the original immediate writes and replacement store reads, not an explicit universal deadline for persistent work.
- The public sources establish synchronous subscriber execution, but do not specify general navigation precedence or renderer, scheduler, or cleanup reentrancy.
- Exception recovery, cancellation races, mutable non-string inputs, and ordering of independent actions at identical deadlines are unspecified.
- Attempt 1 supplies passing syntax checks and an acceptance verdict without behavioral observations. It establishes neither causality nor exhaustive correctness or cross-task benefit.
- The related experiences' submission, projection, immutable-copy, and buffer-bank rules may apply to their original sources; their absence here does not disprove those rules.
- This guidance is provisional; effectiveness is unknown.

Verify timer resetting, no active-burst write before 120 ms of quiet, one latest-text write per burst, later successful bursts, empty text, and no-selection editing. With pending edits, exercise switch, same-document reopen, close, and disposal; verify original-document persistence before return and fresh replacement reads. Exercise timer-driven and departure-driven subscribers that open or close the editor and then edit the successor; check successor rendering and independent saving without duplicate consumption. Specifically arrange a subscriber before the status listener that closes or reopens the view during notification: the captured retired status callback must produce no output, including on same-document reopen. Confirm preview's unchanged 40 ms delay, hide cancellation, and subsequent reuse. These checks operationalize TASK's "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." and the cited public source behavior; they are not claims about observed acceptance coverage.

rules.body: Apply when introducing trailing persistence into a synchronous editor whose save listeners can navigate. TASK requires "after a 120 ms quiet interval write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts must continue to save." README.md requires "Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text." These requirements make persistence boundaries and visit identity part of preserving supported behavior.

Keep the visit's immutable in-memory text current immediately, then push it into that visit's reusable trailing task. Preserve pending edits at departure and before submission capture rather than canceling them. Preserve the utility's clearing of pending state before invoking work: src/workflow.rb contains "    @handle = @pending = nil\n    @work.call(value) unless value.nil?" This allows edits admitted by a save callback to form an independent subsequent batch.
